## Further Reading

Vasarhelyi, M. A., and Halper, F. B. (1991). The continuous audit of online systems. *Auditing: A Journal of Practice and Theory*, 10(1), 110-125. This foundational paper introduced the concept of continuous auditing and argued that accountants need systematic methods for summarizing and monitoring large volumes of transactional data. The descriptive analytics techniques in this chapter, including automated summarization and threshold-based flagging, are practical implementations of the monitoring approach the authors envisioned.

AICPA (American Institute of Certified Public Accountants). (2017). *Guide to audit data analytics.* AICPA. This professional guidance document describes how auditors can use data analytics throughout the audit process. The sections on stratification and population profiling are directly relevant to the techniques taught in this chapter and provide additional context on how descriptive analytics supports audit planning and risk assessment.

Bradbard, D. A., Alvis, C., and Morris, R. (2014). Spreadsheet usage by management accountants: An exploratory study. *Journal of Accounting Education*, 32(4), 24-30. This study surveyed management accountants about their spreadsheet practices and found that data summarization was among the most common uses. The paper provides evidence that the PivotTable and aggregation skills taught in this chapter are directly aligned with the skills most frequently required in management accounting practice.

Sledgianowski, D., Gomaa, M., and Tan, C. (2017). Toward integration of Big Data, technology, and information systems competencies into the accounting curriculum. *Journal of Accounting Education*, 38, 81-93. This paper argues that accounting curricula should integrate data analytics tools such as PivotTables and conditional aggregation within the accounting context rather than teaching them as isolated technical skills. The approach taken in this chapter, where every function and PivotTable is applied to an accounting question, reflects the integrated pedagogy the authors recommend.

Peecher, M. E., Schwartz, R., and Solomon, I. (2007). It's all about audit quality: Perspectives on strategic-systems auditing. *Accounting, Organizations and Society*, 32(4-5), 463-485. This paper discusses the role of professional judgment in the audit process, including the importance of developing well-informed expectations before performing analytical procedures. The paper supports this chapter's emphasis on interpretation and communication as essential complements to the technical work of summarization.

IMA (Institute of Management Accountants). (2019). *IMA Management Accounting Competency Framework.* IMA. This framework identifies data analysis and interpretation as core competencies for management accountants. The descriptive analytics skills covered in this chapter, including data summarization, variance identification, and trend analysis, are directly mapped to the competency areas the framework describes.

Earley, C. E. (2015). Data analytics in auditing: Opportunities and challenges. *Business Horizons*, 58(5), 493-500. This paper provides an overview of how data analytics is transforming audit practice, including the shift from sample-based testing to full-population analysis. The stratification and descriptive profiling techniques taught in this chapter are entry points into the full-population analytics approach the paper describes.

Appelbaum, D., Kogan, A., and Vasarhelyi, M. A. (2017). Big Data and analytics in the modern audit engagement: Research needs. *Auditing: A Journal of Practice and Theory*, 36(4), 1-27. This paper outlines a research agenda for the use of data analytics in auditing, including descriptive analysis of transactional populations. The authors argue that descriptive profiling should be a standard component of audit planning, which supports the inclusion of stratification and population analysis exercises in this chapter.
